title: Do Personality-Tuned LLMs Make Better Social Agents?
abstract: arXiv:2609.21857v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used in social simulations for socially interactive agents and robots, offering more flexibility than rule-based systems. However, even though they mimic human behaviour very well, there is a persistent alienness to them. This work investigates whether personality-aware fine-tuning can reduce this gap by improving the consistency and controllability of personality-conditioned dialogue generation compared with instruction prompting alone. We fine-tune two small open-weight LLMs, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Ministral-8B-Instruct, using a corpus that combines personality-labelled social media posts and dialogues to create a personality-based dialogue engine for social simulation. The resulting models are evaluated across multiple social interaction scenarios using three independent LLM judges, which assess personality fidelity and provide evidence-based behavioral interpretations. translated_title: 人格调优的大语言模型能成为更好的社交智能体吗？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被用于社交交互智能体和机器人的社会模拟中，相比基于规则的系统提供了更大的灵活性。然而，尽管它们能很好地模仿人类行为，却始终存在一种难以消除的疏离感。本工作研究了人格感知的微调能否缩小这一差距，即与仅使用指令提示相比，能否提高人格条件对话生成的一致性和可控性。我们使用结合了人格标注社交媒体帖子和对话的语料库，对两个小型开源大语言模型 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 和 Ministral-8B-Instruct 进行微调，构建了面向社会模拟的基于人格的对话引擎。所得模型在多个社交互动场景中由三个独立的大语言模型评审进行评估，这些评审衡量人格保真度并提供基于证据的行为解释。此外，我们还量化了评审者之间的一致性。
tldr: 本研究通过结合人格标注的社交媒体帖子和对话语料对小型开源大语言模型进行人格感知微调，证明相比单纯的指令提示，微调能显著提升人格条件对话生成的一致性与可控性，从而减少社交模拟中智能体的疏离感。
en_tdlr: This study fine-tunes small open-weight LLMs on a corpus of personality-labelled social media posts and dialogues, demonstrating that personality-aware fine-tuning improves the consistency and controllability of personality-conditioned dialogue generation over instruction prompting alone, thereby reducing the alienness of LLM-based social agents in social simulations.
